author: Jennifer Salazar
title: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) Position Trimmed by First Quadrant L P CA
text:
Posted by Jennifer Salazar on May 4th, 2018 // No Comments
First Quadrant L P CA trimmed its holdings in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 17.5% during the fourth quarter, according to the company in its most recent filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission. The institutional investor owned 817,578 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 173,629 shares during the period. Apple comprises approximately 2.6% of First Quadrant L P CA’s holdings, making the stock its 2nd largest holding. First Quadrant L P CA’s holdings in Apple were worth $138,359,000 as of its most recent SEC filing.
Several other institutional investors and hedge funds have also made changes to their positions in AAPL. Crow Point Partners LLC raised its position in shares of Apple by 100.0% during the 3rd quarter. Crow Point Partners LLC now owns 1,000 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $153,000 after acquiring an additional 500 shares in the last quarter. Oak Point Wealth Management acquired a new stake in shares of Apple during the 4th quarter valued at approximately $163,000. Interactive Financial Advisors acquired a new stake in shares of Apple during the 4th quarter valued at approximately $188,000. JJJ Advisors Inc. acquired a new stake in shares of Apple during the 3rd quarter valued at approximately $201,000. Finally, Hikari Power Ltd acquired a new stake in shares of Apple during the 3rd quarter valued at approximately $208,000. 61.18% of the stock is currently owned by institutional investors. Shares of AAPL stock opened at $176.89 on Friday. The company has a current ratio of 1.24, a quick ratio of 1.20 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74. Apple has a fifty-two week low of $142.20 and a fifty-two week high of $183.50. The stock has a market capitalization of $858,015.69, a price-to-earnings ratio of 19.21, a PEG ratio of 1.29 and a beta of 1.26.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last issued its earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share for the quarter, topping the consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. Apple had a return on equity of 39.33% and a net margin of 21.55%. The company had revenue of $61.14 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $60.94 billion. During the same period in the prior year, the firm posted $2.10 EPS. The business’s revenue was up 15.6% compared to the same quarter last year. equities research analysts expect that Apple will post 11.28 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
The company also recently announced a quarterly dividend, which will be paid on Thursday, May 17th. Shareholders of record on Monday, May 14th will be given a $0.73 dividend. This is a positive change from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a yield of 1.65%. The ex-dividend date is Friday, May 11th. Apple’s dividend payout ratio is presently 27.36%.
Apple declared that its Board of Directors has approved a share buyback plan on Tuesday, May 1st that authorizes the company to buyback $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This buyback authorization authorizes the iPhone maker to buy up to 11.9% of its shares through open market purchases. Shares buyback plans are often an indication that the company’s board believes its stock is undervalued.
Several research firms recently issued reports on AAPL. Vetr lowered Apple from a “strong-buy” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $187.18 price target on the stock. in a research report on Wednesday, February 14th. Zacks Investment Research raised Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $197.00 price target on the stock in a research report on Thursday, January 18th. Rosenblatt Securities restated a “buy” rating and set a $180.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research note on Friday, March 16th. Monness Crespi & Hardt started coverage on Apple in a research note on Wednesday, April 11th. They set a “buy” rating and a $235.00 price objective for the company. Finally, Goldman Sachs started coverage on Apple in a research note on Wednesday, February 7th. They set a “neutral” rating and a $161.00 price objective for the company. One investment analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-three have issued a buy rating and two have assigned a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. Apple presently has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus target price of $204.00.

The stock was sold at an average price of $174.66, for a total transaction of $6,833,048.52. Following the transaction, the insider now owns 64,475 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $11,261,203.50.
